s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with rash and hypotension in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: erythematous patches and thin plaques with telangiectases and hyperpigmentation
key_facts: patient has a history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis
patient was being treated with fluconazole
pembrolizumab treatment was stopped due to a morbilliform reaction
new skin eruption appeared different from previous reaction
patient has fever and hypotension
white blood cell count is 4100/μL
absolute neutrophil count is 2940/μL
hemoglobin level is 8.2 g/dL
platelet count is 62 ×10^3/μL
blood culture results showed no growth at 1 week
serum β-D-glucan, galactomannan, Coccidioides antibody, and immunodiffusion results were negative

shortlist.label: Intravascular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: skin biopsy showing intravascular atypical cells

shortlist.label: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: febrile illness with rash and hypotension in an immunocompromised patient

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: new skin eruption appeared different from previous reaction

shortlist.label: Natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: patient has a history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis and was being treated with fluconazole

shortlist.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: patient has fever and hypotension with a low white blood cell count

raw.rationale: The patient's skin biopsy findings, including hematoxylin-eosin stained sections and CD56 immunostaining, showed intravascular atypical cells, which is consistent with intravascular large B-cell lymphoma. The patient's symptoms, such as fever, hypotension, and rash, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Intravascular lymphoma
rejected.why: Too broad, as intravascular large B-cell lymphoma is a more specific diagnosis that fits the patient's presentation

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's skin biopsy findings do not support this diagnosis, and the presence of intravascular atypical cells is more consistent with a B-cell lymphoma

rejected.label: Natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and biopsy findings do not support this diagnosis, which is more commonly associated with nasal or extranodal disease

rejected.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and biopsy findings do not support this diagnosis, which is more commonly associated with systemic symptoms, lymphadenopathy, and a distinct immunophenotypic profile
